paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We measure the average similarity between models fine-tuned on random subsets S and single-task models. We observe that the similarity score becomes lower as the size of S increases.

model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates how cosine similarity varies with the subset size \(|S|\) for two methods (“Weight averaging” and “QAdapter”). The x-axis is labeled \(|S|\) and uses a linear scale spanning integer values from 2 to 10, with labeled ticks at 2, 4, 6, 8, and 10. The y-axis is labeled “Cosine similarity.” and uses a linear scale ranging from about 0.1 to 0.5, with labeled ticks at 0.1, 0.3, and 0.5. The “Weight averaging” series is shown as a blue dashed line with filled square markers; it decreases across the x-range, from approximately 0.48 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.32 at \(|S|=10\), passing through roughly 0.42 (\(|S|=3\)), 0.39 (\(|S|=4\)), 0.35 (\(|S|=6\)), and about 0.33 (\(|S|=8\)). The “QAdapter” series is shown as a green dashed line with filled circular markers; it also decreases across the x-range, from approximately 0.38 at \(|S|=2\) to about 0.20 at \(|S|=10\), with intermediate points around 0.29 (\(|S|=3\)), 0.27 (\(|S|=4\)), 0.22 (\(|S|=6\)), and about 0.20–0.21 from \(|S|=7\) through \(|S|=10\).
